title: Arrangers for Celestin
summary: Arrangers included Cecil Thornton from St. Louis, Henry Holloway, and Fats Pichon. The band used mostly special arrangements, with some stock.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Any questions, Rob? I have one more. Who were some of the arrangers that wrote for Celestan?

There was a fellow from St. Louis who was very good by the name of Cecil. I can't remember his last name right now, but Cecil was one who was hired especially for arranging. Then there was one named Henry Holloway. Kildee. Kildee. Kildee. He was a member of the band. He was very good as an arranger. And we used to buy arrangements from Fats Pichon.
So he used to write arrangements?
Oh, he was, yes. He was a very good arranger. And he used to buy arrangements from various people, but these three were outstanding as arrangers.
He didn't use stock arrangements, no?
We used stock, but we would especially run. Yes, add some more courses. Yeah, yeah.
He is some stock, but mostly specials.
What about Adolf Alexander Sr., did you ever play any of his arrangements? No, not Tats, but his father.
I just wondered. Did you know a fellow named Thornton that wrote arrangements? He played saxophone, played tenor, I think, from out of St. Louis.
Cecil Thornton, that's the fellow of whom I'm speaking. Very good arrangement.
